markets.question: Will it be confirmed that a problem with the FAA's SMART air traffic management system caused the FAA's nationwide ground stop on Nov 13? · SMART AI system
markets.displayTitle: Will it be confirmed that a problem with the FAA's SMART air traffic management system caused the FAA's nationwide ground stop on Nov 13? · SMART AI system
markets.rules:
If a Source Agency confirms after Issuance and before Dec 1, 2026 that a problem with the FAA's SMART air traffic management system caused the FAA's nationwide ground stop on Nov 13, then the market resolves to Yes.
This must be confirmed, verified, or established as factual by at least one Source Agency.

The ground stop is the nationwide departure ground stop the FAA ordered on Nov 13, 2026. A cause counts if a Source Agency reports it as a cause of the ground stop or of the radio, radar or other system outage behind it. More than one market can resolve to Yes.

Equipment or system failure: a malfunction of hardware, software, power or telecommunications equipment used by the FAA or its contractors, including one set off by maintenance work or accidental damage. A cyberattack, jamming or sabotage is not a failure.
Maintenance or upgrade work: planned maintenance, an upgrade, a configuration change or a cutover on an FAA or contractor system
Cable cut or physical damage: accidental damage to a cable, line, antenna or other physical equipment, including by construction work or weather
Software or configuration error: a fault in software, or a wrong setting or configuration, in an FAA or contractor system, including one introduced by an update or upgrade
Telecom carrier or contractor fault: the failure, damage, error or work behind the outage was in equipment, a network or a system run by a company other than the FAA, such as a telecommunications carrier or an FAA contractor
SMART AI system: a malfunction or error in, or the deployment or rollout of, the FAA's SMART air traffic management system, including its interaction with other FAA systems
Human error: a mistake by a person, such as an FAA employee, air traffic controller, technician or contractor, set off the outage, including a wrong command, setting, procedure or physical action. A deliberate act meant to disrupt equipment or operations does not count.
AI tool or agent error: an AI system or AI agent (a machine-learning model, large language model or autonomous agent) itself produced the action, output or change that caused the outage, and the Source Agency describes that system as AI. It does not count if AI was only part of the affected system, used by staff or contractors, running at the time, or used to help write software that later failed.
